messages:
Ella Torres: Hey @Marco — to escalate quickly we need a minimal repro. Short checklist (smallest items first):

1) Minimal curl that reproduces the failing API call (include full request headers). Example:
```
curl -v 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -H "x-redwood-request-id: <if present>" 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -d '{"input":"..."}'
```

2) HAR file from Chrome/Edge devtools (Network -> right-click -> Save as HAR). If using Android WebView, remote debug with chrome://inspect and Save as HAR.

3) SDK debug token or logs (set SDK log level DEBUG, or capture the SDK debug token shown in the Console/SDK trace output). Include the exact SDK version.

4) Time window (UTC) when you saw the error, and the user/session id if available.

If headers are missing (common when an edge/proxy strips them), include the HAR + a curl replay. If you can only do one thing, HAR is best because it contains request/response headers + timing. Thanks — that will let us find the trace on our side faster. :thumbsup:

Marco Ruiz: Thanks — quick q: how do I get this from our Android app? It's a WebView that hits our proxy, and we often only see a 502 in the app.

Ella Torres: Two quick ways for Android WebView:
- Use chrome://inspect -> inspect the WebView -> Network tab -> reproduce the call -> right click request -> Save as HAR.
- If you can't remote debug, enable SDK debug logging (set env var or SDK flag to DEBUG) and reproduce; paste the debug token string or the last 20 lines of logs.

Also: check for headers named `x-redwood-request-id`, `x-request-id`, or `x-correlation-id`. Some customers run edge proxies (CloudFront, Fastly) that may strip custom headers — if that's the case send the HAR + proxy config snippet.

Marco Ruiz: I tried but the response headers are gone. I can run a curl from our staging host. What's the best curl to run to capture everything?

Samir Patel: If headers are gone in the client, run a curl with verbose trace to capture raw request/response bytes. Example (saves trace to a file):
```
curl --trace-ascii trace.txt -v 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -d '{"input":"short repro text"}'
```
Then attach `trace.txt` and the exact wall-clock time you ran it. If you can't share auth creds, mask the token but keep the header name.

If your proxy rewrites host/headers, also include the proxy request/response snippet (we've seen CloudFront Lambda@Edge do rewrites).

Olivia Chen: Quick attach checklist for the escalation ticket (so we can hand to eng):
- HAR (preferred) OR curl trace.txt + curl command used
- SDK logs or debug token (include SDK version and platform)
- Approx UTC time window + sample session id or user id
- Short notes: what you expected vs what happened (e.g., 502 + empty body, latency spike ~800ms)

If size/privacy is a concern, redact bodies but keep headers and timing. If you must redact, mark which fields were removed.

Marco Ruiz: OK sending HAR + the curl trace in a sec. Do you need console screenshots?

Ella Torres: Screenshots of the Console request inspector are helpful but not required. If you have Console -> Request History showing a session reference or request id, screenshot that and note the timestamp.

Marco Ruiz: Uploading now. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

escalation-bot: Escalation created: ENG-1123 (assigned: eng-oncall). Attachments: har_2026-03-17.har, trace.txt

Samir Patel: Got the HAR and trace, pulling logs now. If we need more, we'll ask for a mini repro payload (trim input to 1–2 tokens) so we can replay without sharing customer data.

Olivia Chen: Thanks @Marco — leaving notes on ticket re: proxy stripping suspicion. We'll update once engineering confirms the trace. :white_check_mark:
